question.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t>0$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{{t}^{3}},\,4t,\,-7⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
question.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{{t}^{3}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-7)⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{t},\,4,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $v\times a,||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨\sqrt{t},\,4,\,0⟩\times ⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,0,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \sqrt{t} & 4 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} & 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{t} & 0 \\ \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{t} & 4 \\ \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,-\frac{2}{\sqrt{t}}⟩, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(\sqrt{t})}^{2}+{(4)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{t+16}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(0)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{t}})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{2}{\sqrt{t}})}{\sqrt{t+16}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{t(t+16)}}.\end{aligned}
$$
